text:
ashley: heads up — we're seeing apiserver 503 bursts in us-east-2 after a GPU preemption storm. controller-manager leader flips every ~30s and scheduler shows large bind/retry latencies. noticed a pile of etcd tombstones and compact lag.

samir: seeing same. metrics: apiserver latency p99 jumped to 1.2s, errors count +4k in 10m. GPU node pool autoscaler kept replacing nodes which made churn worse. :grimacing:

anya: logs from apiserver show a lot of watch reconnects and exceedable fd counts. suspect kube-proxy or calico fragmentation on the node-level mtu mismatch after new AMI rollout. paste of kv watchdog: 

infra-bot: [alert] apiserver_5xx_rate > 0.05 for 5m in us-east-2

michael: (I mean miguel) can we surface etcd leader metrics? are tombstones piling on leader or followers?

samir: quick dump from etcd: 
```
etcdctl --endpoints=https://10.2.1.8:2379 endpoint status --write-out=table
ID	VERSION	DB_SIZE	IS_LEADER	RAFT_INDEX
... 
8a7f	3.5.0	2.1GB	true	1342342
b2c3	3.5.0	2.09GB	false	1342339
c4d5	3.5.0	2.08GB	false	1342330
```
and tombstone/GC backlog on follower c4d5: pending tombstones ~42k entries, compaction lag ~12m

anya: that matches the controller-manager logs: 
```
E0318 14:02:12.123 controller-runtime/manager.go:xxx] failed to sync object: Watch closed: resourceVersion too old
```

ashley: timeline — new GPU AMI rolled 13:45, preemption wave 13:58, autoscaler replaced ~80 nodes by 14:10, apiserver errors spike 14:12.

miguel: I suspect two interacting issues: (1) node churn causing watch cache invalidations and high RAFT traffic; (2) network MTU mismatch on the new AMI causing larger kubelet/kube-proxy timeouts and TCP retransmits -> slows etcd replication.

samir: agree. quick mitigation proposal: pause node autoscaler for the GPU pool, cordon remaining preemptible nodes, and increase apiserver max-fds and etcd election timeout temporarily. Also enable etcd compaction and snapshot faster.

anya: +1 to pause autoscaler. I'll run a rolling restart of kube-proxy on a few nodes to see if MTU clears (but need change window).

ashley: can someone run these commands? I'll own the pause autoscaler bit.

samir: running now — disabling autoscaler for pool 'gpu-preemptible-us-east-2': 
```
kubectl patch clusterautoscaler ca-gpu -n kube-system --type merge -p '{"spec":{"paused":true}}'
```

infra-bot: autoscaler patch applied by samir at 2026-03-18T14:25:01Z

miguel: also bumping etcd election timeout from 1000ms -> 2500ms in the controlplane helm values and restarting etcd-statefulset one at a time:
```
helm upgrade controlplane ./charts/controlplane -f values.yaml --set etcd.electionTimeout=2500
```

anya: restarted kube-proxy on 3 nodes in the affected AZ, monitoring packet drops / retransmits.

samir: triggered a manual compaction snapshot at 14:33: 
```
etcdctl --endpoints=https://10.2.1.8:2379 snapshot save /tmp/snap.db
etcdctl --endpoints=https://10.2.1.8:2379 defrag
```

ashley: good. early signs show apiserver 5xx declining, leader flips reduced to ~2-3 min. still some tail latency.

miguel: action items: 
- validate AMI network stack changes and revert if wrong (miguel/infra-eng)
- add a preflight check to node AMI rollout to validate MTU and kube-proxy configs (devex)
- make autoscaler reactive to controlplane-health signals to avoid replacement storms (samir/product)
- tune etcd compaction schedule and increase snapshots retention temporarily (eng-sre)

anya: also note cost blast — autoscaler replaced 80 nodes, ~24 GPU-hours of spot spend. finance heads-up queued.

ashley: I'm going to keep the autoscaler paused for 1h and follow up in next infra sync. if apiserver looks stable in 30m we'll uncordon nodes slowly. thanks all. :thumbsup:

miguel: tagging @platform-eng to verify AMI patch gating for next rollout.

infra-bot: incident ticket created: INC-2026-0318-42 (assigned to eng-sre).
